name: Salt Lake City
blurb: Utah's capital and largest city, home to Temple Square and the state's government and economic center.

name: West Valley City
blurb: Utah's second-largest city, a diverse suburb west of Salt Lake City known for the Maverik Center arena.

name: West Jordan
blurb: A fast-growing Salt Lake County suburb along the Jordan River near South Towne-area retail.

name: Provo
blurb: Home to Brigham Young University, Provo is Utah County's seat and anchors the Provo-Orem metro area.

name: Orem
blurb: A Utah County city bordering Provo, nicknamed 'Family City USA' and home to Utah Valley University.

name: Sandy
blurb: A Salt Lake County suburb at the foot of the Wasatch Range near the Alta and Brighton ski resorts.

name: St. George
blurb: The seat of Washington County and hub of Utah's 'Dixie' region, known for red-rock scenery and rapid growth.

name: Ogden
blurb: Weber County's seat, a historic railroad town at the mouth of Ogden Canyon near the Wasatch Mountains.

name: Layton
blurb: Davis County's largest city, home to part of Hill Air Force Base and a major retail corridor.

name: South Jordan
blurb: An affluent, rapidly developed Salt Lake County suburb along the Jordan River.

name: Lehi
blurb: A booming Utah County tech hub nicknamed 'Silicon Slopes' for its concentration of tech company offices.

name: Millcreek
blurb: A Salt Lake County city incorporated in 2016, sandwiched between Salt Lake City and the Cottonwood Canyons.

name: Taylorsville
blurb: A Salt Lake County suburb along the Jordan River, incorporated in 1996.

name: Herriman
blurb: One of Utah's fastest-growing cities, a Salt Lake County suburb on the valley's southwest edge.

name: Logan
blurb: Cache County's seat and home to Utah State University, in the mountain-ringed Cache Valley.

name: Murray
blurb: A centrally located Salt Lake County city with its own school district and hospital, nicknamed the 'Hub of Salt Lake Valley.'

name: Draper
blurb: A Salt Lake County city spanning toward Utah County, known for the Point of the Mountain and its tech campuses.

name: Bountiful
blurb: A Davis County city overlooking the Great Salt Lake from the benches of the Wasatch Range.

name: Riverton
blurb: A Salt Lake County suburb along the Jordan River known for its rodeo and growing residential development.

name: Spanish Fork
blurb: A Utah County city at the mouth of Spanish Fork Canyon, known for its annual Fiesta Days rodeo.

name: Roy
blurb: A Weber County suburb between Ogden and Hill Air Force Base.

name: Pleasant Grove
blurb: A Utah County city at the base of Mount Timpanogos, home to the annual Strawberry Days festival.

name: Cedar City
blurb: Iron County's seat, home to Southern Utah University and the Utah Shakespeare Festival.

name: Kaysville
blurb: A Davis County city known for its historic downtown and proximity to Hill Air Force Base.

name: Cottonwood Heights
blurb: A Salt Lake County city at the mouth of Big and Little Cottonwood Canyons, gateway to several ski resorts.

name: Holladay
blurb: A Salt Lake County city surrounded by Salt Lake City and other suburbs, incorporated in 1999.

name: Eagle Mountain
blurb: One of the fastest-growing cities in the U.S., a Utah County suburb in the Cedar Valley.

name: Saratoga Springs
blurb: A rapidly growing Utah County city on the shore of Utah Lake.

name: American Fork
blurb: A Utah County city near the mouth of American Fork Canyon and Timpanogos Cave National Monument.

name: Park City

name: Heber City
blurb: Wasatch County's seat in the Heber Valley, a gateway to Deer Valley and Jordanelle Reservoir.

name: Midway

name: Moab

name: Vernal
blurb: Uintah County's seat, a Uinta Basin town known for its dinosaur fossil heritage and energy industry.

name: Price
blurb: Carbon County's seat in Castle Country, historically built around coal mining.

name: Tooele

name: Brigham City
blurb: Box Elder County's seat near the Bear River Migratory Bird Refuge.

name: Richfield
blurb: Sevier County's seat, a central Utah trade hub along Interstate 70.

name: Kanab
blurb: Kane County's seat near Zion and Bryce Canyon, long used as a filming location for Westerns.

name: Hurricane

name: Washington

name: Ephraim
